title: The Hooded Confessor
text: A hooded confessor sits in the cathedral's darkest booth, hearing the city's sins day and night for nothing, never seeming to tire. He remembers every one. Now he has begun to write them down in a great black book, in a very neat hand.

options.label: Let him hear the city's sins; a city unburdened sleeps easier.

outcomes.text: The city sleeps easier, and the black book grows.
Pages of his book turn up nailed to doors. One carries a House's name, with a sin the House thought buried.

options.label: Seize his black book before someone worse reads it.

outcomes.text: The book is a ledger of every House's secrets. Each House takes its own page, and reads the others'.
There is no book, and there never was a confessor. The booth smells of wet earth. That night every House's sins are whispered in its halls.

options.label: Leave him to his booth; confession is between a soul and its confessor.

outcomes.text: In spring he leaves by the road toward the Gate, heavy with secrets. Whatever waits there will read them.
